title: Type Conversion and Casting in C++
learningObjectives: Explain the key idea in type conversion and casting in c++.
Identify the relevant syntax and rules.
Trace each example and predict the result.
Apply the concept in a small program.
Avoid a common mistake related to this topic.

understand.concept: Type conversion changes a value from one type to another. C++ performs some conversions implicitly, while explicit casts communicate intent. Narrowing can lose information, so prefer clear initialization and check conversions when data may exceed a target type's range.
understand.whyItMatters: Conversions occur in arithmetic, assignments, input handling and API calls. Understanding them prevents surprising results.
understand.analogy: Think of this as a control or calculation rule that tells a program how to handle a particular situation consistently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a starting point; C++ syntax, types and execution rules determine actual behaviour.
understand.explain:
## Implicit conversions
The language may convert operands to a common type for an operation or convert an initializer to a target type when allowed.

## Explicit conversions
Use a named cast such as `static_cast<double>(count)` to make a conversion clear. Avoid C-style casts in new C++ code because they hide the conversion category.

## Narrowing
Converting a larger or fractional value to a smaller integral type can lose information. Braced initialization rejects many narrowing conversions at compile time.

examples.explanation: The explicit cast converts the integer value to double.

examples.title: Fraction truncation
examples.explanation: Converting to int discards the fractional part; it does not round.

examples.title: Common arithmetic type
examples.explanation: The integer is converted for the mixed arithmetic expression.

examples.title: Safe explicit intent
examples.code: int items{3};\ndouble each{2.25};\ndouble total = static_cast<double>(items) * each;
examples.explanation: The conversion makes the intended numeric type visible.

examples.title: Avoid narrowing brace init
examples.code: // int value{3.7}; // narrowing error\nint value = static_cast<int>(3.7);
examples.explanation: Braced initialization diagnoses narrowing; an explicit cast states intent but still loses the fraction.
